name: Wirtshaus Kematsried
kurzbeschreibung: Entry not confirmed as a Tyrolean business: the coordinates point to Oberjoch/Bad Hindelang in the Allgäu (Bavaria, DE).
beschreibung:
Overview

In the present JSON, the entry “Wirtshaus Kematsried” is assigned to the region Ausserfern in Tyrol and provided with the coordinates 47.5194, 10.4077. However, a review based on the available evidence shows that these coordinates and the sources found point to the locality of Oberjoch in Bad Hindelang in the Bavarian Allgäu (Germany) – and not to a municipality in Tyrol (Austria). The source jungholz.tirol, the destination website of the Tyrolean municipality of Jungholz, even lists the business explicitly under the “Allgäu” category. The business therefore cannot be confirmed as a Tyrolean catering establishment within the meaning of this portal, and the region “Ausserfern” stated in the entry does not match the actual location.

History/Background

The assignment to Tyrol is apparently based on geographical proximity: Jungholz is a Tyrolean exclave that can be reached via the neighbouring Allgäu and the Tannheimer Tal, and the Jungholz tourism page also reports on businesses in the immediate surroundings beyond the state border. The border area between the Ausserfern, the Tannheimer Tal and the Allgäu has been closely connected in alpine farming for centuries; place and field names ending in “-ried”, “-joch” and “-schwand” are common in this mountain region and refer to cleared pastureland as well as mountain passes. However, no reliable history of a Tyrolean business supported by official Tyrolean sources can be documented for the “Wirtshaus Kematsried”, since the location lies outside the borders of Tyrol. For a correct record, the actual municipality and its tourism association would first need to be responsible.

Getting there

Arrival “in Tyrol” is not possible for this business because it administratively belongs to the Bavarian Allgäu. In general, the border area is accessible via the German B 310 road and the A 7 motorway (Oy-Mittelberg exit), as well as via the Tannheimer Tal on the Tyrolean side (Reutte, Weißenbach, Schattwald) and the municipality of Jungholz. Those using public transport depend on the regional bus network of the adjacent Bavarian and Tyrolean valleys; business-specific arrival, public transport or parking details are deliberately not included here as long as no verified Tyrolean source is available.

Tips

Since the entry is not located in Tyrol, it should not be published for a Tyrolean tourism portal as long as no clear location within the state borders has been proven. For future research, it is advisable to check the address, postcode and area code – the domain ending “.tirol” alone is not sufficient as evidence, since it can also list businesses close to the border outside Tyrol. The coordinates should always be reconciled with the verified address via official geocoding.

Best time to travel

For the Allgäu-Tyrol border area, the summer months from June to September as well as the winter season with winter sports are usual. A business-specific indication of the best time to travel is not possible due to the lack of a verified Tyrolean source and is therefore not claimed.
